newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ALPINE SKIING-CONCUSSION SIDELINES SEIZINGER FOR THREE DAYS.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-CONCUSSION SIDELINES SEIZINGER FOR THREE DAYS.

text.p: Olympic downhill champion Katja Seizinger has been ordered to rest for three days after suffering mild concussion in a crash during Saturday's World Cup race.
Seizinger, the overall World Cup champion, was preparing to start in Sunday's slalom -- the final event before the world championships -- when German team doctors ordered her to pull out.

The 24-year-old German had appeared unhurt after getting to her feet and skiing down the piste following her high-speed crash in the downhill. But doctors said on Sunday that she had concussion and needed to rest.

The injury is not expected to affect Seizinger's world championship preparations. She was due to travel to Sestriere with her team mates after Sunday's slalom but was not due to race until the women's giant slalom next Sunday.
